newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria to pay Brady bond coupon in January.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria to pay Brady bond coupon in January.

text.p: Bulgaria will pay some $130 million interest on its Brady bonds due on January 28 next year despite the financial crisis and lack of external support, Finance Minister Dimitar Kostov said on Thursday.
"Foreign debt payments due in January are not very big and we will have the means to cover them," Kostov told a news conference.

Bulgaria issued on July 28, 1994 three types of Brady bonds with a total par value of $5.1 billion as part of a restructuring deal on its $8.16 billion commercial debt to the London Club of creditor banks.
Failure to meet reform targets including closing or restructuring state enterprises has led to the suspension of funding from the World Bank and the International Monetary Fund.
Bulgarian central bank reserves stood at $525 million in November.
The IMF has proposed the introduction of a currency board, a tight monetary regime which is expected to boost confidence in the crumbling lev.
Under the system, the central bank will not be able to print levs it cannot cover with hard currency reserves, and this is expected to remove political pressure from monetary policy.
The system will be introduced after parliament passes next year's budget and a package of legal amendments which would make the currency board operational.
Kostov said Bulgaria needed to have the legal amendments ready by mid-January so that the currency board plan can be introduced by mid-Feburary.
IMF experts who have been discussing technical details of the currency board are due to leave on Friday after presenting a draft report to the central bank.
An IMF negotiating mission must discuss the proposal with the government when details are finalised early next year.
